subject: Follow-up: Competitive trial & incident SLA probing — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara O'Neill <sara.oneill@acme-data.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04 13:02 PDT
Subject: Follow-up: Competitive trial & incident SLA probing — next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary goals: (1) evaluate per-token latency under realistic qps, (2) validate failover behavior and RCA timelines during an incident, (3) confirm data residency and access controls for PII workloads.
- You're running a mixed workload: short chat (<=128 tokens) and long-form summaries (~1k tokens) with peak bursts up to 40 qps.
- Current shortlist: Redwood inference, BigCloud's managed inference, and HyperscaleCorp's endpoint.

What we propose (concrete, timeboxed):
1) Competitive SLA matrix: we'll share a one-page comparison of support tiers, guaranteed time-to-first-response, RCA windows, and SLO credits for model-serving incidents.
2) Trial plan (2-week sandbox):
   - Phase A (functional): correctness and latency baselines on your golden prompt set.
   - Phase B (stress + incident sim): synthetic latency spike + controlled node failover to observe warm vs cold KV cache effects and failover amplification.
   - Acceptance criteria: 99th pct latency under target, failover recovery < 3 minutes for dedicated variant, documented RCA steps.
3) Security artifacts: we'll queue our SOC2 summary, dataflow diagram, and a short runbook showing how we surface logs/traces for incident triage.

Action items for Acme:
- Share golden prompt set (5–10 examples) and a small request trace sample (redacted) so we can size cache/kv params.
- Confirm which support SLA matters most: first-response SLA (eg 1h) vs full RCA delivery (eg 72h).
- Let us know applicable procurement timelines.

I've attached a draft competitive_sla_matrix.xlsx comparing Redwood vs BigCloud vs HyperscaleCorp for the typical incidents you called out. Also attached is a high-level trial runbook.

Attachments: [Attachment: competitive_sla_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)], [Attachment: redwood_trial-runbook.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

We can schedule a short sync next week to finalize the test plan — I propose Tue 10/6 10am PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Sara O'Neill <sara.oneill@acme-data.com>

Date: 2026-10-04 15:10 PDT
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive trial & incident SLA probing — next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few points from our side:

Priorities
- Incident handling & RCA cadence is number one. Our compliance team requires a documented RCA within 72 hours for sev-1 customer-impacting events.
- Secondary is predictable latency for our 95/99p target across mixed sequences.
- Third is data residency — any log/trace export must remain in our US tenant and be access-controlled.

On competitors — we've already seen a 3-hour degraded state with BigCloud last quarter where automatic failover didn't bring latencies back to acceptable levels quickly; we'd like to quantify that behavior across vendors rather than rely on anecdotes.

Deliverables we need from Redwood
1) A short incident-response playbook that shows how your team interfaces with customers, typical timelines (first response, mitigation, full RCA), and who is looped in for infra vs product RCA.
2) Any contract language or SLA bullets around credits (percentage/timeframe) for availability / degraded performance.
3) Confirmation that trial instances can be in our US-only VPC and that logs will be retained per our policy (30 days by default).

We'll put together the golden prompt set and a redacted trace. We can do Tue 10/6 10am PT for the sync — please send a calendar invite.

Sara O'Neill
Director, Data Platform
Acme Data

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara O'Neill <sara.oneill@acme-data.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05 09:20 PDT
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive trial & incident SLA probing — next steps

Sara —

Appreciate the specificity — that helps. Quick responses inline and next steps.

1) Incident-response playbook: attached is a short playbook and an incident-runbook tailored to inference incidents (high token-queueing, KV cache cold starts, model fallback). It lists the expected communication cadence we commit to for each severity:
   - Sev 1 (customer-impacting): first response <= 1 hour, mitigation update every 30 minutes, full RCA draft within 72 hours, final RCA with timeline and root cause analysis within 7 business days.
   - Sev 2: first response <= 4 hours, RCA within 10 business days.

2) SLA language: we included a comparative table in the attached competitive_sla_matrix.xlsx that surfaces credit policies and escalation paths. Short summary: Redwood provides prioritized on-call for Dedicated customers (1h pager) and a documented RCA process that includes stack traces, kernel-level logs (where permitted), and a timeline of events. For hosted tier we offer 4h first response; Dedicated adds the 1h option and a named escalation contact.

3) Trial infra: we can spin a trial in your US-only VPC or in our private trial environment with logs forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/s3. Retention defaults to 30 days but we can extend per request.

Proposed competitive incident tests (to run during Phase B):
- Test A: Controlled node drain — observe failover time and 95/99p latency delta (warm vs cold KV).
- Test B: Synthetic traffic spike — verify autoscaling and how request throttling vs backpressure is applied.
- Test C: Simulated zone outage (if you want to be aggressive) — measure cross-region failover and session continuity.

Attachments: [Attachment: incident-response-playbook.docx (docx, 68KB)], [Attachment: competitive_sla_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]

I looped in Laura (Solutions Eng) — she will own the test harness and artifacts. Jonas (Ops) will propose a technical checklist for the node-drain test. We'll prepare a short set of success metrics and a runbook by EOD Mon.

Confirming Tue 10/6 10am PT — I'll send the invite. Anything else you'd like on the agenda?

Best,
Ben
